items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Casper Hostein, I know him, the number man.

ctx.x: Yeah. That was it, babe. We called it cold kina (PHONETIC), that was the name of it, cold kina. Cold food, they called it cold kina. I had a drawer full of turkey and ham and potato salad. Never opened the drawer if there was some strangers there or somebody come that wasn't a close friend of mine. Ain't going to never pull that drawer out.
Did you ever meet -- there was a rich guy up in Harlem during those years who was kidnapped at one time, Casper Holstein (PHONETIC).

Casper Hostein, I know him, the number man. Yeah, he was one of the few colored guys -- he was a numbers back-up. They kidnapped him, sure. But they turned him loose because he was closely associated. 'Cause they put the word out, "turn him loose." Whenever the Syndicate says, "that's my man," that was it. That was it.
